content: The Regional Office aims to strengthen its collaboration with national interagency coordinating committees (ICCs) and regulatory committees within Member States. This effort is intended to optimize the use of expertise and improve coordination within these states. The Regional Office will also explore opportunities to enhance cross-border collaboration between WHO regions, particularly in outbreak response and through the MECACAR platform. Participants in the MECACAR platform will include WHO headquarters, the WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), UNICEF, the United Nations Foundation, and the ministries of health in the targeted countries. Revitalizing MECACAR as a platform for coordinated activities could significantly contribute to achieving the 2015 measles and rubella elimination goals. This will involve shared communication and data exchange, coordinated outbreak response and immunization activities, identification of mobile populations crossing borders, and support for Member States to maintain political commitment. To secure the necessary resources, the Regional Office plans to establish a funding source for revitalizing the MECACAR platform by June 2014. Additionally, a cross-border coordination meeting between the European and Eastern Mediterranean regions will be organized by June 2014 to develop and endorse a Joint Measles and Rubella Activity Plan. The Regional Office has initiated a verification process to document progress toward measles and rubella elimination. This process began in 2012–2013 with the establishment of the Regional Verification Commission for Measles and Rubella Elimination, the development of a Strategic Framework for Elimination, and the organization of four regional intercountry meetings in collaboration with ECDC and WHO headquarters. Member States are responsible for collecting, analyzing, and interpreting epidemiological and laboratory data on measles, rubella, and congenital rubella syndrome (CRS). They must also ensure the adequacy of their surveillance systems. Progress is assessed through annual status reports submitted to the Regional Office, with the first reports due by the end of July 2013. Despite recognizing the importance of the verification process, Member States often lack the necessary resources, and the process is sometimes perceived as an additional burden for national programs and ministries of health. Support from the Regional Office and other partners is essential to sustain the required efforts for verification activities. Technical assistance visits will be provided to selected Member States by epidemiology and communication staff from the Regional Office. Priority countries will be chosen annually based on factors such as timely submission of annual status reports and the ability to establish a functioning National Verification Committee (NVC). The Regional Office will also motivate Member States by highlighting best practices and providing feedback on progress toward elimination. This feedback will serve as an incentive for performance improvements. Milestones include technical assistance visits to 3–5 Member States per year, the production of a report summarizing outcomes of the four intercountry meetings held in 2012–2013, and annual Regional Verification Commission meetings followed by the publication of meeting reports. Training sessions will be conducted to strengthen immunization systems, including training national coordinators on strategies like Reaching Every District and mid-level immunization management. Vaccine management assessments and follow-up missions will also be carried out in priority countries. Efforts will be made to improve case-based surveillance systems, integrate rubella-related surveillance, and ensure the accreditation of at least 95% of national measles/rubella laboratories in the WHO Europe laboratory network. The Regional Office will publish a manual on vaccine safety risk management and conduct subregional training sessions on vaccine safety at national and subnational levels. Training packages for measles and rubella will be developed and accredited for continuing medical education. Advocacy efforts will include high-level visits to priority countries and roundtable meetings to address challenges and opportunities related to measles and rubella elimination. The Regional Office will also strengthen online media platforms, leverage blogger networks, and develop new technologies to enhance communication and engagement. This includes launching immunization reminder/tracker apps in multiple languages and supporting Member States in improving their immunization-related web content. Finally, responsive vaccine communication assistance will be provided to priority Member States, including support for awareness campaigns, risk communication, and social mobilization efforts. Reports will be produced for each country, outlining recommendations and outcomes of the support provided.
